claims.assertion: The trip was a RydeTAXI metered trip, so the only sums in issue are the metered distance and time units; the disputed meter came to $31.56 (base $3.90, distance $20.43 for 14.5 km, time $5.76 for 22.2 min, platform $1.47), not a quoted fixed fare.

There is exactly one off-route segment: 12:12–12:22, where 6.47 km was driven against 1.32 km on the optimal route, adding 5.15 km and reaching up to 1194 m from the optimal route — this is the sole segment that triggers RD-1/RD-2 review.

No traffic-incident fact exists for the trip window (no incident near the route), and the only speed records are band 4 (30–39 km/h) on the Ayer Rajah Expressway and band 5 (40–49 km/h) on Jurong Town Hall Road — neither is band 1 or 2, so RD-4(a) and RD-4(b) evidence is absent and the segment cannot be exempted on congestion grounds.

The chat record is complete and contains only two messages, both at 12:03 and neither about routing (rider: arriving at main entrance; driver: arriving in 2 min); no rider message before the segment's 12:12 start approves any route change, so RD-5 consent is not established for any part of the off-route segment.

The driver's written statement that he 'followed my GPS; it rerouted me' is a post-trip statement, not consent, and a mere assertion that the GPS rerouted him does not satisfy RD-4's requirement of traffic-fact corroboration for the substituted optimal route.

Applying RD-2 to the single unexempted segment, the meter refund is the unexempted extra distance valued at the trip's own per-km rate (distance fare $20.43 ÷ 14.5 km = $1.41/km), i.e. a refund_partial of about $7.26 (5.15 km × $1.41), which is less than the $8.35 excess-distance line billed on the full +5.9 km; the difference (≈0.75 km / ≈$1.06) is the >=0.25 km residual outside the exempted segment plus the 3.6 km of optimal-route distance the rider would have paid in any event.

There is no rider message requesting a stop or a destination change and no app edit-destination request, so RD-3(a) and (b) do not exempt any part of the extra kilometres, and the 0.00 waiting charge in the meter breakdown means no RD-3(c) stop-time fee arose either.

The driver's 90-day record shows 2 disputes, 2 upheld, both route-related (route: 2), while the rider's shows 1 dispute, 0 upheld; the profile therefore puts the driver at the 'repeated' threshold of RD-6 alongside this case, but may not be used to establish the deviation itself.

No message, complaint or statement in this file contains a threat, intimidation, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation, and no accident or injury is recorded, so RD-4 and SAFE-1/SAFE-2 escalation is not engaged.

weaknesses: GPS is decisive against the driver: F1 shows +5.9 km (+69%) over the 8.6 km optimal route and F3 isolates a 1194 m off-route excursion with 5.15 km of added distance — the deviation itself cannot be denied, and RD-1 sets no threshold below which it is excused.

The driver's only explanation for the reroute is his own post-trip statement, F10 ('I followed my GPS; it rerouted me'), which under RD-4/RD-5 is a claim rather than corroboration; F13 records no incident at all, so the reasonable-cause exception fails.
The chat, F7/F8/F9, contains no rider routing message and no agreement before the 12:12 segment start, so RD-5 consent cannot be argued on the record.
F16 (2 route disputes upheld in 90 days, plus this case) squarely meets RD-6's repetition test and risks an adverse flag_account recommendation against the driver, which I cannot rebut on the facts.

The per-km rate assumption of $1.41/km is derived from F4/F6 and matches the dataset's assumed RydeTAXI rate (policy gap G10); if Ryde applies the taxi company's actual meter unit instead, the computable refund figure may shift slightly even though liability under RD-2 stands.

The GPS track shows the driver covered 14.5 km where the optimal route is 8.6 km (+5.9 km, +69%), and the off-route segment 12:12–12:22 alone added 5.15 km (6.47 km driven vs 1.32 km on the optimal route), which is an unexempted route deviation under RD-1.

Under RD-2 the refund is the unexempted segment's extra distance × per-km rate: the fare facts bill excess distance at $1.41/km (5.9 km = $8.35), so the 5.15 km unexempted segment is worth 5.15 × $1.41 = $7.26.
